# `Tins::IP.ttl` Field

In the **libtins** C++ network packet crafting and sniffing library, `Tins::IP::ttl()` refers to the **Time To Live** field in an IPv4 header.

## What is TTL?

The **Time To Live (TTL)** is an 8-bit field in the IPv4 header that:

- **Limits the lifespan** of a packet on the network
- **Decremented by 1** at each router/hop the packet passes through
- When it reaches **0**, the packet is **discarded** and an ICMP "Time Exceeded" message is sent back to the sender
- Prevents packets from circulating indefinitely in case of routing loops

## Usage in libtins

```cpp
#include <tins/tins.h>

using namespace Tins;

// Creating a packet and setting TTL
IP ip_packet = IP("192.168.1.1") / TCP(80, 1234);

// Get the TTL value
uint8_t ttl_value = ip_packet.ttl();

// Set the TTL value
ip_packet.ttl(128);
```

## Common Default TTL Values

| OS | Default TTL |
|---|---|
| Linux | 64 |
| Windows | 128 |
| macOS | 64 |
| Cisco IOS | 255 |

## Typical Uses

- **Traceroute**: Sends packets with incrementally increasing TTL values to discover each hop
- **OS Fingerprinting**: The initial TTL value can help identify the sender's operating system
- **Network diagnostics**: Analyzing TTL values helps debug routing issues
